title: Phase host run behavior
statement: Let $M_i$ be the machine assigned to each phase $i$, let $q_0$ be an initial state in the disjoint union of the phase state sets, and let $\mathrm{red}$ assign to each phase state either no redirection or a new phase state. Fix a phase $i$, an input word $x$, configurations $c,c'$ of $M_i$ on $x$, a choice word $w$, and a state $s'$ such that running $M_i$ from $c$ under $w$ gives $c'$ with state $s'$. Suppose $\mathrm{red}(i,s')=q'$ for some phase state $q'$, and that at every prefix of $w$ of length strictly less than $|w|$, whenever the run of $M_i$ from $c$ under that prefix has state $s$, one has $\mathrm{red}(i,s)=\varnothing$. Then, for every prefix length $u\le |w|$, the phase-host machine run from the phase-tagged configuration $c$ under the first $u$ bits of $w$ agrees with the run of $M_i$ under that prefix, with states tagged by $i$; moreover, for every bit $b$, its run under $w$ followed by $b$ ends at the configuration $c'$ with its state replaced by $q'$.
hypotheses_covered: A family of machines $M_i$ indexed by a type $I$.
A redirection function returning either no redirect or a phase-tagged state.
An input word $x$ and configurations $c,c'$ for $M_i$ on $x$.
A choice word $w$ with $M_i$ run under $w$ from $c$ equal to $c'$.
A state $s'$ such that $c'$ has state $s'$.
At every prefix length $u<|w|$, the run state, if present, has no redirection.
